subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Grade 10 Capstone: Personal Activity Plan and LEVEL 1 Transition
essentialQuestion: What have I built that is worth specializing in?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of consolidating two years of LEVEL 1 evidence in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe self-assessment against the five standards using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply identifying the strongest and weakest of the five for the learner in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving choosing a LEVEL 2 specialization direction and justifying it; correct it and explain why.
Connect planning access, equipment, and time for that direction with setting the safety and self-management rules that carry forward and explain how one affects the other.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Present a LEVEL 1 completion file and a justified LEVEL 2 specialization proposal to one trusted adult, and revise the proposal after critique.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
